findings.issue: The long-string data slot is printed as the folded keccak constant (with 63 digits, P6) instead of sha3(5) / sha3(6), the allocation size of the returned copy is the obscure 'floor32(_3 - 97) + 128', and the memory-to-memory copy into the return buffer stays a while loop (P7).
findings.rule: Keep keccak(slot) symbolic for a storage string's data (print stor5[0 len n]); a loop 'mem[d + i] = mem[s + i]' step 32 to n is a copy line; floor32(x + 160 - 97) for x = 32 * k + 160 is ceil32 arithmetic that can fold to the string's padded size.

notes: Reviewed against FarmingPool.sol, FarmAccounting/UserAccounting libraries, 1inch SafeERC20 and OZ ERC20/Ownable (via-IR build). All 25 ABI functions were read (690 lines): deposit/withdraw/claim/exit with the farmed-amount checkpointing, transfer/transferFrom with the per-user checkpoints, startFarming/stopFarming with their distributor checks and reward transfers, rescueFunds. The pack lists no source loop and the text has only the two string copies of name/symbol as while loops (P7). Immutable staking/rewards tokens read as 0 (artifact, const STAKING_TOKEN/REWARDS_TOKEN = 0). No execution run.
summary: Clean and faithful; only the string getters show defects (folded keccak data slot, opaque allocation size, a copy left as a while loop).
